copy.summary: The offer is clear on the home page ("Industrial design meets fashion. Atypical leather goods") and product descriptions are specific, but delivery and return terms contradict each other across four pages. Several issues (placeholder contact details, mixed brand names) come from deliberate Dawn demo content.
strengths: Product descriptions on the 3 sampled bags state shape, material, size contents and use, e.g. the Studio Bag fits "wallet, phone, 500ml water bottle, and sunglasses".
Home page headline and sub-headline state what is sold: "Functional handbags made of luxurious materials".
All 15 rendered pages carry lang="en" and the copy is in English throughout, with no spelling errors found on the sampled pages.
Add to cart, Buy it now and Sold out buttons say what happens next.

design.summary: Dawn is visually clean and consistent: one logo, one type family, and buttons, cards and headings that behave the same on home, collection, product and cart, with a strong hero and generous galleries. The real gaps are invisible ones (no alt text on any product image, the logo as the share image on the home page) plus faint footer text. This is Shopify's deliberate Dawn demo store, so the demonstration notice on product pages and the placeholder brand are intentional and not reported.
strengths: Every product has several photos: 0 of 32 products have no image or a single image, ranging 5 to 25 images each (shop/catalogue-stats.json, shop/products.json)
The home page has no horizontal overflow on phone (pages/home/phone.json, horizontalOverflowPx 0)
Product pages set the product photo as the sharing image (pages/products-helix-denim/desktop.json seo.ogImage)
Page language is set to "en" and no image has a missing alt attribute or is broken on any of the 15 pages tested

growth.summary: This is Shopify's Dawn demo store, so the near-empty measurement set-up (Shopify analytics only, no ad pixels, no social links) is expected rather than a fault. The points that would matter on a live store are missing barcodes/SKUs for Shopping feeds and the lack of ad and consent set-up.
strengths: No console errors and no failed requests on any of the 14 pages (pages/*/desktop.json console and network)
Add to cart works with correct product on all 5 tested product pages (clicktest/results.json)
Internal links carry no utm_ parameters, so real traffic sources are not overwritten (pages/*/desktop.json links)
Product pages have a single canonical URL, one H1 and valid structured data (ldInvalid 0)

products.summary: This is the Dawn demo store, so the catalogue is small and tidy: 32 priced products with 8 to 25 images each, real descriptions, and compare-at prices that are always above the price. The gaps are housekeeping: sold-out items leading the home page, a Sale collection that is not about sales, blank product types and SKUs, and no image alt text.
strengths: Every product has at least 5 images (min 5, max 25) and a description of at least 371 characters (shop/products.json)
Only 29 of 266 variants (5 products) carry a compare-at price, and none is equal to or below the price, so the sale badge keeps its meaning (shop/catalogue-stats.json)
The announcement bar, product page and shipping page all say shipping is free, so there is no threshold to compare to the median price of 460 CAD (pages/home/text.txt)
Add to cart clicks on the 5 tested product pages added the right product, and no upsell interrupted the purchase (clicktest/results.json)

qa.summary: Buying works: all 10 add-to-cart clicks (5 products, phone and desktop) put the right product and variant in the cart, and no page shows console errors, failed requests or broken images. The two faults found are small and both sit on policy pages: a cut-off size table on phone and a dead link in the returns text.
strengths: 10 of 10 add-to-cart clicks on 5 in-stock product pages (phone and desktop) reached the cart as the right product and variant (clicktest/results.json, verdict MATCH)
0 console errors, 0 failed requests and 0 broken images on all 15 rendered pages (pages/*/desktop.json)
66 of 67 internal links and all checked external links resolve (links.json)
14 of 15 phone pages have no sideways scroll (horizontalOverflowPx 0) and the only fixed bar is the 65px header (pages/*/phone.json)

tech.summary: Technical basics are solid: one h1 per page, canonicals on every sampled page, Product structured data on all 5 product pages, all 32 products in the sitemap and no third-party apps loading. The main gaps are bare home and collection metadata and a 3.3 s lab LCP on the phone home page; this is Shopify's demo store, so some content is deliberate.
strengths: All 32 products from products.json appear in the sitemap (64 product URLs incl. variants/duplicates checked, 0 missing)
Product pages carry ProductGroup structured data with no invalid JSON-LD (ldInvalid 0)
Product page phone lab LCP is 2.2 s with CLS 0 and TBT 128 ms
No third-party apps or trackers beyond Shopify analytics were detected on the pages checked

trust.summary: Strengths are free shipping stated in the header on every page, a real founder story with a quality promise, and a footer email sign-up. The gaps are missing policy pages and footer links (the /policies/ URLs return 404), inconsistent shipping and returns details, and no reviews or back-in-stock option; much of this is deliberate demo content.
strengths: A "Free shipping available on all orders!" bar shows at screen 1 on all 5 product pages checked
The About page names a founder, a start year (2015) and a "quality promise" with a take-back line
A contact page with phone, email, address and a contact form exists; a Returns page states a 14-day window and condition rules
Footer has an email sign-up and social links; none of 14 pages triggered a pop-up on phone

ux.summary: The demo store is easy to read: the home page says what it sells in the first screen ("Industrial design meets fashion.", "Atypical leather goods", one "Shop now" button), there are no pop-ups, and Add to cart worked as expected on 5 of 5 products tested. The friction is small: sold-out items lead the home grid, Add to cart sits just below the first phone screen with no sticky bar, and there is no social proof near prices. Much of this is likely deliberate demo content.
strengths: Home first screen on phone shows a clear headline, sub-headline and one primary CTA "Shop now" (pages/home/phone-first.jpg)
No pop-ups on any of 15 pages on phone, and none after 12 seconds (INDEX overlays column, pages/home/phone-after-12s.jpg)
Add to cart matched the product on 10 of 10 clicks (5 products, phone and desktop); a notification offers View cart, Check out and Continue shopping (clicktest/results.json)
Collection pages offer Filter (Availability, Price, Color) and 9 sort options; the header has Bags, Shoes, Lookbook, a search icon and cart on phone (pages/collections-bags/text.txt)
Sold-out and unavailable variants are struck through and the sold-out product page shows a disabled Sold out button (pages/products-small-convertible-flex-bag-cappuccino/phone-first.jpg)

findings.title: Delivery time is stated three ways: "2-4 business days", "1-4 days after shipment" and "5-10 business days"
see_it: Open https://theme-dawn-demo.myshopify.com/pages/shipping: it says "Delivery takes between 2-4 business days depending on your location" and a 2-business-day wait for the shipping notification.
Open https://theme-dawn-demo.myshopify.com/pages/shipping-returns: it says "We ship all US domestic orders within 5-10 business days".
Open https://theme-dawn-demo.myshopify.com/products/helix-denim, section after the description: "You'll receive your order an estimated 1–4 days after shipment."

evidence.note: "2-4 business days" plus up to 2 days for the notification email
"5-10 business days" for US domestic
"estimated 1–4 days after shipment"

findings.why_it_matters: A buyer cannot tell whether an order arrives in about a week or in two. Three different promises mean support questions ("where is my order?") and a risk that the shortest claim is the one the buyer relies on when deciding. The shipping-returns page is also reachable only by direct URL, so shoppers see the two shorter promises and later may find the longer one.

fix.summary: Pick one real delivery window per region and use it on the shipping page, the product-page block and the announcement bar.
steps: Decide the true handling time and transit time per region.
Rewrite the Shipping page, the product-page "Free Shipping" block and delete or fix the Shipping & Returns page.
State handling and transit separately (e.g. dispatch in X days, delivery in Y days).
fix.where_to_change: Online Store > Pages > Shipping, Shipping & Returns; Themes > Customize > Product page > Shipping block

findings.claude_prompt: Store https://theme-dawn-demo.myshopify.com. Three pages give different delivery times: /pages/shipping "2-4 business days", /pages/shipping-returns "5-10 business days" for US domestic, product pages "1-4 days after shipment". I will give you the true handling and transit times per region. Draft one consistent wording for each of the three places and list the exact pages and theme blocks to edit. Work on a duplicate theme, show me the diff before publishing, do not touch checkout.
findings.verify_fix: Search each page for "days": every delivery claim now matches the single agreed window.

findings.title: Return terms disagree: "free returns", a 14-day return window, and free home-collected exchanges are described on different pages
see_it: Open https://theme-dawn-demo.myshopify.com/pages/shipping-returns: "Free shipping and returns available on all orders!"
Open https://theme-dawn-demo.myshopify.com/pages/returns: return within 14 days, unused, original packaging; it does not say who pays return postage or mention a free collection.
Open a product page (e.g. /products/helix-denim): "Hassle-Free Exchanges ... We will collect from your home, work or an alternative address." Only exchanges are mentioned, not refunds.
Open https://theme-dawn-demo.myshopify.com/pages/about: "If our product doesn't satisfy you, we'll take it back." with no time limit.

evidence.note: "Free shipping and returns"
14 days, original packaging, no mention of return cost
"Hassle-Free Exchanges" with home collection
"we'll take it back" with no window

findings.why_it_matters: Buyers of a 400+ CAD item look for a clear refund promise. Here the free-returns claim, the 14-day window and the collect-from-home exchange are never reconciled, so a shopper cannot tell if returns are free, who collects, or whether they get money back or only an exchange. That raises pre-purchase hesitation and returns disputes.

fix.summary: Write one returns policy that covers window, refund versus exchange, who pays shipping, and pickup, and reuse its wording on product pages and About.
steps: Decide the facts: window, refund/exchange, return postage, pickup.
Update the Returns page, delete or align the Shipping & Returns page, and edit the product-page "Hassle-Free Exchanges" block and About text.
fix.where_to_change: Online Store > Pages > Returns; Themes > Customize > Product page
